parsed.explanation: Adult alone: federal passport/visa screening is traveler-facing; binary marker rules, X-marker elimination, discrepancy checks, denial, and possible permanent ineligibility create severe border exposure. Protective state/provincial law gives strong facilities, anti-discrimination, hate-crime, and care recourse, lowering everyday local risk. But federal immigration custody, national corrections, and youth-care funding pressure remain operative overrides. Adult with minor is worse because public coverage for gender-affirming youth care suspends and hospital/care compliance is contested. The combined regime is therefore high risk: local protections work against street and facility harm, but cannot offset border, federal custody, or minor-care exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal policy mandates binary sex assigned at birth, eliminates new X markers, and treats document/appearance discrepancy as grounds for refusal, additional screening, or fraud-based permanent ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; courts and civil-liberties litigation contest the regime, and a legal-aid FAQ assists with markers, but no traveler immunity is documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatched documents can escalate to denial, stranding, fraud allegation, or custody; state/provincial protections do not bind federal consular or immigration screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration custody involves documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, and severe sexual abuse; national corrections adopts hormone removal, forced haircuts, and conversion-style treatment.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State/provincial corrections has a consent decree for expanded care and specialised/voluntary housing; state anti-discrimination and hate-crime law can support complaints, but no federal immigration remedy is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A local arrest or care encounter can move into federal custody where state protections lack operative reach; federal facility rules may also govern government-funded buildings.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: A national executive order restricts government-funded single-sex facilities; many other state/provinces ban identity-congruent facilities, and four criminalise use, with a documented capitol arrest.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province has full bathroom access, anti-discrimination coverage, chosen-name/pro-pronoun duties, uniform options, and prior school restroom rulings; no local facility ban is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State public-accommodation rules likely operate locally, but federal funding and federal-site restrictions may conflict; outcome is uncertain for government-funded settings.

care_services.exposure: National funding pressure suspends state public-insurance coverage for youth gender-affirming care from October 2026; hospital records subpoenas and school-care threats create scrutiny for minors.
care_services.protection: State law protects gender-affirming care and insurance coverage; the highest court ordered a hospital to resume puberty blockers and hormones; adult care and private care remain more protected.
care_services.interaction: A minor or guardian can become a care seeker under federal funding rules; local court remedies do not yet prove they restore coverage or compel compliance.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism documents prioritise groups described as radically pro-transgender; a DOJ memo mentions radical gender ideology; national orders threaten schools, teachers, and LGBTQ youth services.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity; this state/province has hate-crime enhancements, a prior transgender murder hate-crime conviction, and active civil-rights enforcement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat framing can chill complaints and invite scrutiny, while state/local enforcement may provide meaningful recourse for street or facility incidents.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor or guardian may face loss of public coverage for gender-affirming care, national pressure on youth care, unresolved ballot campaigns, and school-sport restrictions.
minors_guardians.protection: State law protects youth care, bans conversion therapy on minors, requires school name/dress accommodation, and has a high-court order directing resumed gender-affirming care.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian access can move through hospitals, insurers, schools, and federal funding conditions; state protections reduce but do not erase coverage and investigation risks.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No current state/province-specific trans violence rate is documented; national hostility, other-state facility arrests, and public-support polling indicate friction could escalate to confrontation or police contact.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State anti-discrimination and hate-crime law, prior murder hate-crime enforcement, and 2025 protections give local victims realistic complaint routes and seem protective.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street encounters are likely mediated locally unless customs, immigration, or federal facilities are involved; federal climate adds uncertainty despite strong local law.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport litigation, federal-order injunctions, November 2026 ballot outcomes, hospital compliance, and restoration of youth-care coverage remain unresolved; federal enforcement practice is variable.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have issued protective rulings, legal clinics provide documentation guidance, ACLU suits and consent decrees show remedy infrastructure, and some state institutions enforce protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Local remedies are real but do not reliably control federal border, immigration custody, funding conditions, or nationwide facility rules; a visitor may face forum-switching before redress.

anchor_checks.comparison: Partly lower than this border-exclusion anchor because protective state facilities and services reduce everyday local harm. Higher because document mismatch can yield permanent ineligibility and credible severe federal immigration custody. Adult alone may resemble routine border exclusion, but the custody pathway makes the combined regime below a pure exclusion case.

Less continuous than this registration/database anchor: border scrutiny is concentrated at entry or secondary screening, and state public accommodations protect access. Still not merely administrative, because federal custody harm, permanent-ineligibility risk, and youth-care funding denial keep it near or below 0.45.

Similar in discretionary secondary screening and possible refusal or return transport, but worse because federal detention harm is documented and passport restrictions are judicially enabled. Stronger local legal protections raise it above many 0.55 cases, yet credible escalation to fraud/permanent ineligibility or federal custody puts it below.

parsed.synthesis: Protective state law makes adult facility, service, and complaint access work locally, but the operative ceiling is federal. A document mismatch can escalate into denial, permanent ineligibility, or federal immigration custody, where abuse is documented; state consent decrees do not reach federal actors. For minors and guardians, national funding blocks public youth-care coverage and creates scrutiny, while local court protection remains contested. The visitor therefore receives meaningful state remedies against street and facility harm but not against border, federal custody, or funding-driven care loss.
